ELBT 5001.title: Biotech Venture Leadership: Navigating Science and Business
ELBT 5001.description: This course develops leadership skills for biotech ventures, blending scientific innovation with business strategy. Students learn to manage interdisciplinary teams, align R&D with market/clinical needs, and make strategic decisions, using case studies from Hong Kong/mainland China’s biotech sector to drive the impact.
cilos: Demonstrate emotional intelligence in leading diverse biotech teams to foster collaboration and resolve conflicts.
Formulate strategic decisions that balance scientific innovation with business objectives in biotech ventures.
Lead interdisciplinary teams to align R&D efforts with market demands in Hong Kong’s and mainland China’s biotech ecosystem.
Design stakeholder communication strategies to secure buy-in from investors, regulators, and partners.
Develop a visionary leadership plan tailored to a biotech startup’s growth objectives.
Apply ethical leadership principles to address dilemmas in product safety and data integrity.

ELBT 5002.title: Biotech Entrepreneurship: Opportunity to Commercialization
ELBT 5002.description: This course equips students with entrepreneurial skills to transform biotech opportunities into commercial ventures. Through business idea generation, market analysis, business model development, and investor pitching, students learn to navigate Hong Kong’s and mainland China’s biotech ecosystem, leveraging case studies and practical exercises to drive innovation from concept to market.
cilos: Analyze biotech market opportunities to identify viable commercialization prospects in Hong Kong and mainland China.
Construct scalable business models for biotech ventures, integrating R&D and market strategies.
Develop go-to-market strategies tailored to Hong Kong’s and China’s biotech and healthcare ecosystem.
Create compelling investor pitch decks to secure funding for biotech startups.
Assess commercialization risks and develop mitigation plans for biotech ventures.
Leverage Hong Kong’s and GBA’s entrepreneurial resources, such as HKSTP and ITF grants, to support venture growth.

ELBT 5003.title: Funding for Biotech Startups
ELBT 5003.description: This course explores funding strategies for biotech startups, focusing on angel investors, venture capital, and government grants. Students learn to craft compelling funding proposals, negotiate terms, and manage investor relations, using Hong Kong’s and mainland China’s financial ecosystem as a backdrop for practical exercises.
cilos: Identify diverse funding sources suitable for biotech startups in Hong Kong’s and GBA’s ecosystem.
Craft targeted funding proposals and pitch decks to attract angel investors and VCs.
Negotiate investment terms to secure favorable equity deals for biotech ventures.
Utilize Hong Kong’s funding resources, including ITF grants, to support startup growth.
Manage investor relations to maintain long-term partnerships post-funding.
Evaluate financial risks associated with biotech funding and develop mitigation strategies.

ELBT 5004.title: Biotech Product Commercialization
ELBT 5004.description: This course covers strategies for commercializing biotech products, from development to market entry. Students learn to navigate regulatory pathways, develop go-to-market strategies, and build partnerships, using Hong Kong’s and GBA’s biotech ecosystem to drive successful product launches.
cilos: Navigate regulatory pathways for biotech product approvals in Hong Kong, China and global markets.
Formulate go-to-market strategies for biotech products.
Design pricing and distribution plans to optimize market entry in Hong Kong’s and China’s ecosystem.
Establish strategic partnerships for product commercialization with existing biotech firms in Hong Kong and China.
Assess commercialization risks and develop contingency plans for market entry.
Plan and simulate a biotech product launch, addressing post-launch challenges.

ELBT 5101.title: Intellectual Property in Biotech Ventures
ELBT 5101.description: This course provides comprehensive training in intellectual property (IP) management within the biotechnology sector, equipping students with essential skills to protect and leverage biotech innovations. Topics include key patent drafting skills, strategies for biotech inventions, trademark and copyright protection for biological products and processes, and navigating IP disputes in Hong Kong's, Mainland China’s and US dynamic biotech ecosystem. Students will explore licensing agreements, technology transfer mechanisms, and global IP frameworks to effectively commercialize biotech IP assets.
cilos: Formulate IP strategies to protect biotech innovations in Hong Kong’s and China’s ecosystem.
Draft patent applications for biotech products, adhering to PCT and local standards.
Negotiate IP licensing agreements to maximize commercial value.
Apply Hong Kong’s, China’s and the US’s IP legal framework to safeguard biotech innovations.
Resolve IP disputes through strategic litigation or alternative methods.
Evaluate the commercial value of IP assets for biotech ventures.

ELBT 5102.title: Legal Frameworks for Biotech Business
ELBT 5102.description: This course provides practical training on legal aspects of daily startup operations in biotech, covering key agreements such as licensing, employment contracts, stock option plans, collaboration, investment, shareholder agreements, and IPO arrangements. Students will explore additional essential items like founder agreements, NDAs, vendor contracts, and compliance checklists at each startup stage - from inception and formation, through growth and funding, to scaling, partnerships, and exit strategies. Using Hong Kong’s, mainland China’s and US legal ecosystem as case studies, participants will gain hands-on skills to navigate risks, draft documents, and ensure smooth progression from kickstarting a venture to achieving IPO.
cilos: Draft founder and incorporation agreements to establish a compliant biotech startup structure.
Negotiate and draft employment contracts and stock option plans for early team hires.
Develop licensing and collaboration agreements for IP and partner operations.
Analyze and mitigate risks in investment and shareholder agreements during funding stages.
Design legal roadmaps for scaling, including ESG and international clauses, up to IPO.
Simulate negotiations for M&A or IPO arrangements to achieve successful exits.

ELBT 5103.title: Applications of AI in Different Biotech Sectors
ELBT 5103.description: This course provides a strategic overview of AI applications and the investment landscape in biotechnology. Designed for future leaders, it covers evaluating AI tools for R&D, understanding the AI biotech startup ecosystem, and making informed investment and strategic decisions, leveraging Hong Kong's position as a tech and financial hub.
cilos: Analyze common AI tools in drug discovery and diagnostics.
Evaluate the general knowledge of AI-driven solutions for personalized medicine.
Handle data processing process for biotech AI applications.
Apply commonly used machine learning models for biotech.
Navigate Hong Kong’s, China’s and the US’s ecosystem for AI integration.
Address ethical and regulatory AI issues in biotech.

ELBT 5104.title: Managing Biotech Projects, Teams and Operations
ELBT 5104.description: This course focuses on managing biotech projects, teams, and operations. Students learn to apply project management methodologies, lead teams, and optimize operational workflows, using Hong Kong’s and mainland China’s biotech industry as a practical case study.
cilos: Apply project management methodologies in biotech projects.
Lead interdisciplinary biotech teams effectively.
Optimize operational workflows in biotech firms.
Manage project risks and resources.
Foster collaboration in biotech teams.
Evaluate project success using metrics.

ELBT 5105.title: Strategic Decision-Making in Biotech Ventures
ELBT 5105.description: This course adopts a case-based learning approach to develop students’ ability to analyze, evaluate, and make strategic decisions in biotechnology ventures. Students work in teams to examine real-world business situations across areas such as venture success factors, leadership decisions, commercialization strategies, and industry challenges. Through structured discussions, presentations, and coaching, students develop critical thinking, decision-making, and communication skills essential for industry success.
cilos: Analyze complex business situations in biotech ventures and identify key decision issues.
Evaluate strategic options and leadership decisions in biotechnology contexts.
Apply interdisciplinary knowledge to support decision-making.
Develop structured and evidence-based strategic recommendations.
Communicate and defend decisions effectively to stakeholders.
Demonstrate teamwork and leadership in collaborative decision-making contexts.

ELBT 6201.title: Biotech Industry Internship
ELBT 6201.description: This internship provides hands-on experience in Hong Kong’s and mainland China’s biotech industry. Students work with startups or established firms, applying entrepreneurial skills to real-world challenges, and reflecting on their professional growth in a comprehensive report. Graded P or F.
cilos: Design a comprehensive biotech venture plan integrating scientific, business, and regulatory strategies.
Work with a multidisciplinary team to develop and refine a biotech startup concept in Hong Kong’s and GBA’s ecosystem.
Evaluate market opportunities and risks for a biotech venture, leveraging Hong Kong’s and GBA’s resources (e.g., HKSTP, ITF).
Develop investor-ready pitch materials to secure funding for a biotech startup.
Apply ethical and regulatory principles to ensure compliance in venture development.
Integrate feedback from industry mentors to enhance venture feasibility.
Present a biotech venture plan to stakeholders, demonstrating entrepreneurial leadership.

ELBT 6202.title: Capstone Project in Biotech
ELBT 6202.description: This capstone course integrates MSc(ELBT) coursework to develop a comprehensive biotech business plan. Students collaborate with biotechnology associations and biotechnology corporates in the region to commercialize innovations, create financial models, and deliver shark-tank-style investor pitches, preparing them to launch ventures in Hong Kong’s biotech ecosystem.
cilos: Develop a comprehensive biotech business plan integrating market analysis, financials, and IP strategies.
Assess and evaluate university-held patents.
Create and deliver persuasive shark-tank-style investor pitch decks.
Incorporate mentor and industry feedback to refine business plans.
Evaluate commercial potential using SWOT and financial modeling.
Demonstrate entrepreneurial leadership in addressing biotech challenges.
